title: Comcast Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates as Peacock Turns Profitable Again; Broadband Losses Widen
excerpt: Adjusted EPS of $1.07 topped the $0.98 consensus on revenue of $29.3 billion; wireless added a record 368,000 lines while domestic broadband lost 144,000 customers.
body:
• Comcast's third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.07 beat the $0.98 consensus estimate, though it fell 4% from a year earlier; revenue of $29.3 billion was roughly in line with expectations.
  • Peacock delivered adjusted EBITDA of $261 million — its second consecutive profitable quarter — as paid subscribers grew 17% to 48 million.
  • Domestic broadband lost 144,000 customers, worse than the roughly 131,000 expected, while wireless added a record 368,000 lines to reach 10.6 million.
  • Universal became the first studio to cross $5 billion at the global box office in 2026, powered by The Odyssey's nearly $1.8 billion; share buybacks stay paused through the planned NBCUniversal and Sky separation.

Comcast beat Wall Street's earnings expectations for the third quarter on Thursday, as a second straight profitable quarter at Peacock and record wireless additions offset deepening broadband losses and a weak quarter at its theme parks. The results underline the split running through the company: the legacy cable business keeps shrinking, while the mobile and streaming bets built on top of it keep growing.

Adjusted earnings per share came in at $1.07, ahead of the $0.98 consensus estimate compiled by Zacks, though down 4% from $1.12 a year earlier. Consolidated revenue fell 6.1% year over year to $29.3 billion, essentially matching expectations; on a pro forma basis that strips out the Versant separation completed in January and the sale of Sky's German operations in May, revenue rose 0.5%. Adjusted EBITDA declined 5.8% to $9.1 billion, net income attributable to Comcast rose 3.5%, and reported EPS increased 7.2% to $0.97. Free cash flow was $4.2 billion, down 14.8% from a year earlier.

Broadband Bleeds, Wireless Surges

The connectivity business remains the pressure point. Comcast lost 144,000 domestic broadband customers in the quarter — more than the roughly 131,000 analysts had expected — as churn rose during pricing transitions and competition from fiber and fixed-wireless rivals intensified. Domestic broadband revenue fell about 4.7% to $6.24 billion, and residential connectivity revenue overall declined 3.5%.

Wireless is the counterweight. Comcast added 368,000 domestic wireless lines in the quarter, its best mobile performance, taking the total to 10.6 million lines — nearly 18% penetration of its residential broadband base. Wireless service revenue jumped 14.7% to about $1.1 billion as free promotional lines convert to paid relationships, and roughly 45% of broadband customers are now on gigabit-plus speed tiers. Business services connectivity revenue rose 2.7% to $2.6 billion, with segment EBITDA up 1.7% to $1.5 billion.

Peacock and the Studios Carry Content

Peacock's adjusted EBITDA of $261 million, against a loss a year earlier, marked the streaming service's second consecutive profitable quarter, and paid subscribers climbed 17% to 48 million. Media segment revenue rose 13% to $5.4 billion, helped by $224 million of incremental revenue from the FIFA World Cup and stronger Peacock distribution. Theatrical revenue surged 76.6% to $1.1 billion behind The Odyssey, which at nearly $1.8 billion worldwide has become Universal's highest-grossing film ever; studios adjusted EBITDA rose 18.6% to $402 million. Theme parks went the other way: revenue slipped 4.4% to $2.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA fell 17.1% to $780 million on softer admissions and heavier promotion in Orlando and Japan, even as the company opened the Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift coaster at Universal Studios Hollywood.

Separation on Track, Buybacks Paused

Comcast said the planned separation of NBCUniversal and Sky into two independent companies remains on track, with $22 million of transaction costs booked in the quarter, and confirmed that the share repurchase pause begun in the third quarter will stay in place through the separation. Capital expenditure was flat at $3.1 billion, and the company paid $1.2 billion in dividends. The shares were choppy around the release — up nearly 2% at first, then about 1% lower in premarket trading — and remain down roughly 26% this year. For Indian-American households, Comcast matters on two levels: Xfinity is the largest US broadband provider, so its pricing and wireless bundles shape household connectivity bills, and Peacock and Universal's film slate are a growing share of what diaspora families stream and watch in theaters.
